attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6 reproduced the exploit against the finished R6 gate: change a historical target's revision from INV-R5.1 to INV-R6, leave every other field alone, refresh the head digest, and the gate stays green. R6's three checks — the revision has a receipt, the CURRENT file exists, the symbol occurs in the CURRENT file — contain no fact about the named revision. Fourth member of the progression: a string exists, then a reference resolves, then a reference is ABOUT this claim, and now a historical reference IDENTIFIES THE RIGHT HISTORICAL OBJECT. Binding it turned up something the round had not gone looking for: INV-R5's receipt records `sha256_16`, a SIXTY-FOUR-BIT PREFIX, while R5.1 onward record the full digest — so targets bind at different strengths and the gate carries the width rather than implying 256 bits everywhere. THE SYMBOL REMAINS UNBOUND and that is stated rather than glossed: checking an old symbol against the current file and calling it historical resolution is the exact move this record exists to stop.
attrs.statement: A defeater against a historical rule binds to the digest that revision's own receipt recorded for the named path, at the width that receipt recorded it. A named symbol or section is NOT historically resolved, because the tree retains digests and not bytes.
